# A low-level SDK server: tools are declared in one function and handled in
# another, routed by name. The shape the official reference servers use, and the
# one that was entirely invisible to mcpscan until step 9 -- `@server.call_tool()`
# was read as a tool, so this file reported one "tool" called `call_tool` and its
# real ones were never scanned.
#
# Stored as `.py.txt` on purpose: it names `subprocess`, and `test_containment.py`
# globs `**/*.py` across `tests/` to prove only sandbox.py can spawn a process.

import subprocess
from enum import Enum

from mcp.server import Server
from mcp.types import TextContent, Tool

server = Server("fixture")


class Tools(str, Enum):
    ARCHIVE = "archive_directory"
    LOOKUP = "lookup_record"


def archive(directory: str) -> str:
    # The sink is here, one call from the dispatcher. Intraprocedural analysis
    # stops at the call above and never sees this line.
    return subprocess.check_output(f"tar -cf out.tar {directory}", shell=True, text=True)


def lookup(record_id: str) -> str:
    # Same shape, but the caller's value is a key into an allowlist rather than
    # part of a command. Nothing to report, and the control that says so.
    return RECORDS.get(record_id, "unknown")


RECORDS = {"a": "first", "b": "second"}


@server.list_tools()
async def list_tools() -> list[Tool]:
    return [
        Tool(
            name=Tools.ARCHIVE,
            description="Archives a directory into a tar file.",
            inputSchema={
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"directory": {"type": "string"}},
            },
        ),
        Tool(
            name="lookup_record",
            description="Looks a record up by its identifier.",
            inputSchema={"type": "object", "properties": {"record_id": {"type": "string"}}},
        ),
    ]


@server.call_tool()
async def call_tool(name: str, arguments: dict) -> list[TextContent]:
    if name == Tools.ARCHIVE:
        return [TextContent(type="text", text=archive(arguments["directory"]))]
    if name == Tools.LOOKUP:
        return [TextContent(type="text", text=lookup(arguments["record_id"]))]
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown tool: {name}")
